text:
alex: Hey team — customer on Private VPC reported SDK TLS handshake failures right after our scheduled cert rotation tonight. Error in their SDK: "x509: certificate signed by unknown authority". They said direct curl from their laptop works, but our SDK inside their VPC fails. I pulled a client log and paste below.

alex: ```
2026-03-15T02:20:11Z ERROR tls: handshake failure: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
stack: github.com/redwood/sdk/tls.Connect

# openssl s_client -connect api.customer.internal:443 -servername api.customer.internal -showcerts
CONNECTED(00000005)
depth=0 CN = api.customer.internal
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
verify return:1
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=api.customer.internal
   i:/CN=Acme Intermediate CA
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
(MISSING INTERMEDIATE IN THIS OUTPUT)
-----END CERTIFICATE-----
```

maria: Can you grab the cert bundle they uploaded to rotator and the rotator audit entry? Sounds like a classic incomplete-chain or wrong order (leaf only). Also confirm they didn't upload a customer-pinned trust bundle on their side.

samir: Rotator audit shows an upload at 2026-03-15T02:12Z for that tenant. Bundle size: 2148 bytes. The uploaded PEM has two blocks but the intermediate appears truncated (looks like a trailing newline was removed). I can pull the stored bundle if you want.

eng-rotator-bot: rotator/audit: tenant=acme-corp rotation_id=rot-20260315-7 applied=2026-03-15T02:12:09Z bundle_bytes=2148 uploaded_by=acme-ops

maria: If the intermediate is truncated HAProxy will still serve the leaf, but clients that validate the chain will fail. Please run these repro steps and paste output:
1) openssl s_client -connect <host>:443 -servername <host> -showcerts
2) openssl x509 -in leaf.pem -text -noout
3) cat leaf.pem intermediate.pem root.pem > bundle.pem; then verify with openssl verify -CAfile root.pem bundle.pem

samir: Also check VPC egress — if the nodes rely on OCSP stapling or need to fetch intermediate from AIA URL, ensure the customer's firewall allows outbound to the CA's AIA or OCSP endpoints. But given the s_client output shows "MISSING INTERMEDIATE" it's likely bundle issue.

kevin: Quick mitigation path: re-upload a corrected full-chain PEM (leaf then intermediate(s) then optional root), rotate/redeploy via rotator, then gracefully reload HAProxy on the Private nodes. Commands:
```
# locally verify bundle
cat leaf.pem intermediate.pem > bundle.pem
openssl verify -CAfile intermediate.pem bundle.pem
# upload via rotator API (example)
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -F "bundle=@bundle.pem" https://rotator.internal/api/v1/tenants/acme/bundles
# on private nodes
sudo systemctl reload haproxy
```

alex: I pulled the stored bundle and it's indeed missing the majority of the intermediate (truncated PEM). I notified the customer to re-upload full chain. Reuploading now, will post results.

maria: After reupload, also clear any HAProxy cert cache if you're using pinned certs or long-lived worker processes. A full reload should be enough but some deploys need a restart.

alex: Reuploaded correct bundle (leaf + intermediate + root), rotator shows new rotation id rot-20260315-8 applied 2026-03-15T02:34:57Z. I reloaded HAProxy on their Private nodes.

alex: Status update: customer confirms SDK now connects, no more handshake errors. :white_check_mark:

samir: Root cause summary for ticket: customer uploaded a malformed/truncated bundle; rotator accepted it but HAProxy served the incomplete chain. Impact: SDKs that strictly validate chain failed (x509 error). Fix: customer re-uploaded correct chain in leaf->intermediate->root order; rotator rotation applied and services reloaded.

maria: Follow-ups: add a sanity check in rotator to verify full chain present and log clear error if intermediate missing, and add a KB article for customers about required bundle order and common pitfalls (CRLF truncation from some editors).

alex: Filed follow-up GH issue: https://github.com/redwood/rotator/issues/1423 — I'll link to the support ticket.

kevin: Nice catch. Closing thread once QA confirms no flaps.
